note: Material claims sampled from the initial plan (assumptions made before research), the seed guides, and Composio's docs. 'Corrected' means the original belief was wrong and the guides now say what the source says.

entries.claim: Approval is only needed if you list the app in the App Directory; otherwise distribution is fine.
entries.check: Official Slack changelog and rate-limit docs (quote-checked)
entries.finding: Non-Marketplace commercially distributed apps get conversations.history / conversations.replies limited to 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request. For an agent that reads channels, unlisted distribution is effectively broken. It is also called the Slack Marketplace now, not the App Directory.

entries.claim: Marketplace review is a light, optional step.
entries.check: Slack Marketplace review guide (quote-checked)
entries.finding: Submission requires 10 or more active workspaces (developer sandboxes don't count); review takes up to 10 business days preliminary plus up to 10 weeks functional.

entries.claim: Composio's managed Slack app is a safe default for agents.
entries.check: Composio Slack toolkit page (quote-checked)
entries.finding: Composio says it 'is working on Marketplace review for the managed Slack app', so the managed app is currently non-Marketplace: expect install warnings, admin-approval friction, and likely the non-Marketplace history limits. Whether the 1/min limit applies to it is unknown (neither Slack nor Composio states it).

entries.claim: Any app used by real merchants needs Shopify app review.
entries.check: shopify.dev distribution docs (quote-checked)
entries.finding: Custom distribution (a single store, or stores in one Plus organization) needs no App Store review; only public distribution via the App Store does. Custom apps can no longer be created in the store admin.

entries.claim: A Composio-hosted Shopify connection can be distributed through the App Store like any other app.
entries.check: Composio's Shopify credential guide vs. Shopify App Store requirement 2.3.1 (both quote-checked)
entries.finding: Composio's flow asks the merchant to type their store subdomain; App Store requirements forbid asking for the shop domain and require install to start from Shopify. That is a likely review blocker, but whether a Composio-hosted connection can pass review can only be confirmed by submitting one.

entries.claim: Partner account required just to build.
entries.check: shopify.dev docs (no explicit statement found); hands-on pending
entries.finding: Apps are now created in the Dev Dashboard or Shopify CLI; the exact account requirement is to be confirmed in the hands-on test.

entries.claim: Approval is light or none for a public OAuth integration.
entries.check: Notion authorization guide vs. Marketplace listing guide (both quote-checked)
entries.finding: Notion's docs contradict each other: the authorization guide says 'The Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review', while the Marketplace guide says a connection 'can be used via its OAuth flow without being listed'. Only a hands-on test with a second workspace settles it. The guide says so instead of picking one.

entries.claim: Basic scopes (name, email) mean no review at all.
entries.check: Google brand verification + verification exemptions pages (quote-checked)
entries.finding: There is no scope review, but brand verification applies to show your name/logo (automated in minutes, can fall back to 2-3 business days of manual review). Internal (same Google Cloud organization) and personal-use apps are exempt from verification.

entries.claim: Any restricted Gmail scope means a security assessment.
entries.check: Gmail scopes page (quote-checked); flagged by two independent reviewers
entries.finding: The assessment is triggered when restricted-scope data is stored on or transmitted through servers. That covers a typical server-side agent, but not every restricted-scope app. The guide states the scenario explicitly.

entries.claim: Drafting replies (gmail.compose) is a lighter, sensitive scope.
entries.check: Gmail scopes page (quote-checked)
entries.finding: gmail.compose and gmail.modify are restricted (only gmail.send is sensitive), so an agent that drafts replies is on the security-assessment track.

entries.claim: Testing mode: up to 100 test users; their grants expire after 7 days; unverified apps get 100 users for the project's lifetime.
entries.check: Google Cloud Help: Audience settings (quote-checked)
entries.finding: All three confirmed verbatim; basic profile scopes are exempt from the 7-day expiry.

entries.claim: Using Composio's callback URI is fine for verification.
entries.check: Google: authorized domains must be verified in Search Console (quote-checked) + Composio white-labeling doc
entries.finding: Inferred from two documented facts: Google requires ownership verification of authorized domains, and you can't verify Composio's domain, so route the callback through your own domain (Composio documents a redirect proxy). Neither Google nor Composio states this combination outright; labelled as an inference in the guide.

entries.claim: Security assessment cost and duration.
entries.check: Google docs publish neither; only a vendor report found
entries.finding: Google publishes no cost or duration. Nango reports 5-20 days and roughly $540-$720/year; shown in the guide as 'Reported', not fact.

entries.claim: The redirect URI to register is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add (Composio's Google credential guide).
entries.check: Hands-on: created a Slack auth config over the API and connected a test workspace
entries.finding: Both URIs are still supported. Composio's Slack toolkit defaults to the legacy …/api/v1/auth-apps/add; the docs recommend …/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback, and that one worked end to end when registered on the app and set on the auth config. Guides keep saying: copy the URI shown for your auth config.

entries.claim: Probing the authorize endpoint with a dummy client tells you whether the provider validates client IDs up front.
entries.check: probe_url on 4 providers (recorded in each guide)
entries.finding: Behaviour differs and matters for debugging: Google redirects to an invalid_client error immediately; Slack returns HTTP 200 with an empty page; Shopify redirects to the store's admin login first (a bad client ID only surfaces after the merchant logs in); Notion redirects to a JavaScript install page regardless.

entries.claim: Seed guides passed the quote check (226/226 quotes found verbatim on live pages).
entries.check: Stricter rule added after the independent code review: every number in a claim must also appear in its quote; re-ran scripts/check-guide.mts on all four guides
entries.finding: 15 claims stated a number their quote did not contain (e.g. a Slack claim citing '29 May 2025' with a quote that had no date; a Notion claim saying 'three credential types' where the page never counts them). 13 were fixed by quoting the sentence that actually holds the number from the same page; 2 had the unsupported number removed. All four guides pass again.

entries.claim: The live agent can research an unfamiliar app and produce a sourced guide within the serverless time limit, cheaply.
entries.check: Dry run on 5 apps with Haiku 5.5 research + Sonnet 5.5 writing, Composio Search for search: Calendly: 48s, $0.07, 8/8 quotes verified, 0 downgraded; HubSpot: 70s, $0.12, 13/15 quotes verified, 2 downgraded; Xero: 55s, $0.07, 5/7 quotes verified, 2 downgraded; Box: 54s, $0.08, 9/10 quotes verified, 1 downgraded; Gmail: 109s, $0.29, 29/30 quotes verified, 1 downgraded
entries.finding: All 5 produced guides in 48-110s for $0.63 total. Failures seen: Xero's docs are JavaScript-rendered, so both the direct fetcher and Composio's fetch tool got ~76 characters per page and the guide leans on fewer sources (5/7 quotes verified). An early run failed because the guide schema is too large for API structured outputs ('compiled grammar is too large'); writing now uses JSON validated by Zod with one repair turn.

entries.claim: A live agent run on Gmail reaches the same conclusions as the hand-checked seed guide.
entries.check: Compared the live guide's verified claims against 10 key facts in the seed guide
entries.finding: 9/10 key facts present (gmail.send sensitive; readonly/modify/compose restricted; security assessment when data is on servers; 7-day test expiry; lifetime cap; internal exemption; brand and domain verification). Missing: the 100-test-user limit. One claim was downgraded by the number rule (it cited a 401 error the quote didn't mention).

entries.claim: A Box Admin must authorize your Client ID in each enterprise that uses your app (live agent guide headline).
entries.check: Independent output review against Box's official page, read from its Markdown source
entries.finding: Wrong for OAuth 2.0 apps. Box requires admin authorization only for JWT and Client Credentials apps; OAuth 2.0 apps need an admin to enable them only where unpublished apps are inactive by default. Root cause: Box's HTML leaves the link text ('JWT or Client Credentials Grant') out of the server-rendered page, so the agent read 'applications using or must be authorized'. Fixed in the fetcher (it now reads the docs' Markdown source) and the Box guide was corrected by hand.

entries.claim: Automatic downgrades flag unsupported claims.
entries.check: Re-ran the checker on all 10 stored guides after fixing it (no model calls)
entries.finding: 3 of 7 downgrades on agent guides were false alarms: 'OAuth 2.0' read as the number 2, an HTTP 401 code read as a quantity, and a quote starting inside a markdown link. The checker now ignores versions and status codes and normalises links; those claims were restored. The remaining 4 downgrades are real: each claim bundles two facts and its quote supports only one.

entries.claim: Prompt changes (coverage checklist, one fact per claim, Composio checklist, larger fetch budget) improve the agent's guides.
entries.check: 5 new runs (Box, Xero, Gmail, Calendly, Asana; $0.70 total) scored with scripts/eval.mts against the stored outputs: evidence metrics plus per-app must-have facts from the output review
entries.finding: Sources read roughly doubled (5-8 to 8-13), agent-owned steps rose from 10-20% to 30-44%, no hands-on time is 'Unknown' any more, the longest scenario label fell from 97 to 48 characters, and 104 of 107 quotes verified. Gmail now covers all 5 must-have facts (was 4), Xero now has its 2026 connection caps. Still missing: Xero's security assessment above 1,000 connections. Box's claims were right, but its summary still overstated admin authorization and was corrected by hand: summaries are not evidence-checked yet.

entries.claim: Create an auth config with auth_scheme: "OAUTH2" (docs example).
entries.check: Hands-on: POST /api/v3.1/auth_configs
entries.finding: Rejected with 'authScheme: Required'. The REST API expects camelCase authScheme.

entries.claim: A Slack app with the right bot scopes is enough for Composio's Slack toolkit.
entries.check: Hands-on: inspected the authorize URL Composio generated
entries.finding: Composio requests the scopes as user_scope (user token). The app must declare them as user scopes too; added as a trap in the Slack guide.

hands_on.what: Agent-written manifest (attempts/slack/manifest.yaml) imported by a human; install to own workspace; Composio auth config; screenshot distribution requirements.
hands_on.result: Agent created the app from a manifest (Slack API, config token), created the Composio auth config (API), fixed two problems it hit (API field name; user vs bot scopes), and a human clicked Allow once. Connection ACTIVE; a channel-list call succeeded. Log: attempts/slack/log.json.

hands_on.what: Create project, add gmail.readonly and see its label, test-mode consent via Composio, screenshot Verification Center.
Dev Dashboard app + dev store via Composio; screenshot distribution choice; confirm account requirement.
Create a public connection; check whether an authorization URL exists before submitting for review.
